item.title: Statement on Faculty Representation in the 2026 Presidential Search
item.author: Eric Vandenberghe
item.description: With a new presidential search now underway, and in keeping with the November 2025 resolution of the Faculty Senate, we request that a member of SACUA or a SACUA designee be included on the Presidential Search Committee. We make this request in the spirit of consultative leadership, democratic principles, and shared governance. Though we genuinely appreciate that multiple faculty members are on the Search Committee, the distinction between faculty selected by the administration and duly elected faculty representatives is both substantive and symbolic. Elected members of the Faculty Senate carry a mandate from the faculty as a whole. They are positioned to solicit and express overall faculty priorities throughout the process. Our position is consistent with longstanding guidance from the American Association of University Professors (AAUP), which holds that presidential search committees should include individuals elected by the faculty, because doing so “broaden[s] the mandate for the candidate who is ultimately selected to become president.” The University bylaws recognize the Senate Assembly’s advisory role on matters of university-wide consequence. A presidential search is among the most consequential such matters the university undertakes. SACUA is ready and willing to engage constructively throughout the search. We ask that the faculty’s elected voice be a part of it. Approved by the Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs (SACUA) on May 30, 2026. Link to PDF

item.title: University Senate Vote Results- April 27, 2026
item.author: Meaghan Blanchard
item.description:
A Faculty Senate meeting took place on Monday, April 27, 2026. The text and vote results of all motions are available here and, individually, below:
  • Motion 1: Resolution Calling for Support for Faculty and Staff Childcare Needs
    • Results: Yes, 1863 (87.9%); No, 256 (12.1%); Abstain, 217 – Motion PASSED
  • Motion 2: A Call for GenAI-Free Zones
    • Results: Yes, 1711 (82.8%); No, 356 (17.2%); Abstain, 269 – Motion PASSED
  • Motion 3: Resolution on the use of Early Decision Admissions
    • Results: Yes, 1364 (76.3%); No, 424 (23.7%), Abstain, 548 – Motion PASSED
  • Motion 4: Resolution in Support of Intersex, Transgender, and Gender-Diverse Students: Inclusive Athletics and Alignment with University Values
    • Results: Yes, 1299 (69.4%); No, 572 (30.6%); Abstain, 465 – Motion PASSED
  • Motion 5: Resolution to Offer Tuition Support to Faculty
    • Results: Yes, 1961 (90.3%); No, 211 (9.7%); Abstain, 164 – Motion PASSED
  • Motion 6: Resolution to Reject Collaboration with the Senior Service College Fellowship Program
    • Results: Yes, 1440 (77.7%); No, 413 (22.3%); Abstain, 483 – Motion PASSED
  • Motion 7: Motion to Update Research Track Faculty Senate Membership Language
    • Results: Yes, 1713 (92.1%); No, 147 (7.9%); Abstain, 476 – Motion PASSED
